title: From Benchmark Validation to Industrial Evidence: A Registered Systematic Map and Nested Evidence Audit of Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence for Rotating-Machinery Fault Diagnosis
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) methods for vibration- and sound-based rotating-machinery diagnosis are often evaluated on benchmark splits whose meaning depends on physical independence, domain shift, target-domain access, leakage control, and reproducibility. This registered study combines a systematic literature map with a nested audit of validation credibility. Searches identified 11,916 records and retained 7,520 unique records; 5,159 entered the full-text population. The operationally defined, non-random nested cohort contained 351 reports. After three retrieval waves, 98 studies were included, 12 excluded, and 241 remained unresolved because complete articles were unavailable. The studies yielded 158 validation experiments. Within this subset, 89 experiments (56.3%) used segment- or sample-level evaluation, 88 (55.7%) had high leakage risk, 31 (19.6%) reached independent component-, machine-, or site-level evidence, and two (1.3%) reached site or field-population evidence. Target-domain data influenced development in 45 experiments (28.5%). Among 77 experiments with an explicit classification-like numeric headline score, 62 (80.5%) reported at least 95%, showing that headline performance did not distinguish validation credibility. Sensitivity analyses preserved the dominance of weakly independent validation. The Industrial Evidence Matrix separates benchmark interpolation, adaptation, domain generalization, and deployment-oriented evidence. All proportions characterize the access-influenced nested subset and are not estimates for the complete literature.
